title: Attorney General of New Mexico

context.text: Both nominees were unopposed in the June 2, 2026 primaries: incumbent Democrat Raúl Torrez received 187,832 votes and Republican Samuel Kane 95,611.
The New Mexico Secretary of State's 2026 General Election candidate list shows two candidates for Attorney General: Raul Torrez and Samuel Isaiah Kane, Sr.

candidates.name: Raúl Torrez
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary.

summary.text: Raúl Torrez is the Democratic incumbent Attorney General of New Mexico, a former federal prosecutor and Albuquerque-area district attorney. His office has prioritized child protection, including suing Meta and Snap, and joined a multistate lawsuit challenging a federal fuel-economy rule.

background.text: Former federal prosecutor and senior adviser in the U.S. Department of Justice; elected district attorney for the Albuquerque metro area before becoming Attorney General.
Graduate of Harvard University, the London School of Economics and Stanford Law School.

priorities.text: Protecting children, including lawsuits against Meta and Snap, investigations of failures in the child welfare system and undercover operations to arrest online predators (office biography).
Adapting consumer protection laws to the online marketplace, improving oversight of higher education and safeguarding natural resources (office biography).

record.text: Announced that the First Judicial District Court entered final judgment against Meta Platforms ordering it to pay $567 million and adopt court-supervised reforms for five years; with a $375 million jury penalty, total exposure is $942 million.
Joined California Attorney General Rob Bonta in announcing a lawsuit against the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration over its final rule weakening fuel economy standards.

candidates.name: Samuel Kane
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Republican primary.

summary.text: Samuel Kane is the Republican nominee for Attorney General. His campaign site describes him as an attorney with decades of experience, and lists priorities including limits on license-plate-reader surveillance, combating methamphetamine and fentanyl crime, opposing unchecked data-center development and investigating utility rate hikes.

background.text: Describes himself on his campaign site as an attorney with decades of experience "fighting for the rights of New Mexicans"; not born in New Mexico.

priorities.text: Protecting privacy: rein in mass surveillance tools such as Flock license-plate readers.
Addressing crime driven by methamphetamine and fentanyl, supporting and equipping officers, and funding programs for at-risk youth.
Enforcing environmental laws fairly, opposing unchecked data-center development, and investigating utility rate-hike practices.

sources.title: Court Orders Meta to Pay $942 Million and Overhaul Protections for Children on Facebook and Instagram in Landmark New Mexico Ruling
Attorney General Raúl Torrez, AG Bonta and Coalition Challenge Trump Administration’s Rollback of Fuel Economy Standards

researchNotes: Slate: confirmed against the New Mexico Secretary of State's 2026 General Election candidate list (candidate portal). Neither candidate has a published issue-by-issue questionnaire, so no issue stances are recorded. Samuel Kane's campaign site gives only a short biography; his background and any public record before this race were not found. Torrez's record items are from his office's own press releases.
